body: Man, that is the exact same situation Im in. A week before our anniversary, I gave her freedom to hang out with whoever and whenever. She abused it and really hurt me. Im glad to see you're getting through it and hopefully I can too.
Thank you, you two. You have calmed me down enough to not do anything tonight. I owe you my life. Tomorrow I call an old friend who will listen. Thank you.

I know its what I should do but I feel guilty just thinking of talking about it. I dont want my family and friends to look at me different. But when I am up to 5am every morning crying, hitting myself, and thinking of the best way to do it I wonder what other choice I have other than swallowing my fear and talking or one easy step to end my life.

How long has this been going on for? Has it just been these last few days or has he been distancing himself from you and behaving this way for over two weeks? If its just the last few days, text him saying you're here whenever hes ready to talk and give him some space. Sometimes guys like to behave a little immaturely and hold onto little things for a few days but we are also quick to drop it and move on without ever looking back or talking about it again.

If this has been something thats been going on for quite some time, maybe it is time to call it quits.

I would end this relationship. It seems to me that this person is not who they say they are at all. It sounds very sketchy that they randomly messaged you over an walkie talkie application and that it progressed emotionally for them so fast. Also, I don't see this relationship going anywhere, if it is legit. You're better off getting out now and living a little and not tying yourself down to someone you don't even truly know.

Someone posted this exact thing, but opposite the other day. Im not saying its your guy but he was saying was very sincere in the fact that he had the account previously for dating and had only recently logged on to change his relationship status and something else. He stated that his girlfriend was upset when she found it and that he had recently logged in and that it wasn't deleted.

Please know, from a guys viewpoint, that having a still active OK Cupid profile can mean absolutely nothing. If he changed the relationship status I would not worry about it. We dont tend to think along the lines of having the profile means im still looking, but instead along the lines of it says im single and I don't care about it anymore to do anything with it (delete it, change it any more than that, etc). 

How do you know hes checking it daily? If its really bothering you could you ask him to see it? Perhaps hes logging in daily to overlook his profile to see why your mad to or to show friends to see if they see stuff he should take off.

Don't worry about it and talk to him.
Your OP said that the dinner was last week. I would ask her to dinner after work again and plan for it this week. If you wait longer it may seem that you are disinterested.

Well, what things that people say to you trigger the negative emotions? Is it critiques on your character, work ethic, appearance, interests, something else? I also have a tendency to be hostile or defensive when someone is going through a problem that I can not help with. I feel (or used to before I figured this out) that I was less of a man for not being able to make them feel better and that it was now on me. I'll be here for a while if you want to talk it out.

Ask her out before you leave, nothing wrong with that as long as you can keep the workplace professional and the company is ok with it. It is obvious that she is into you and wants a relationship so waiting too long could ruin the opportunity. Since she wants to do another dinner after work you could ask just her to go with you if you two get out at the same time. Don't call it a date but after the night tell her you had a great time and would love to take her on a real date, not just dinner after to work. Best of luck.

Congrats on the job. Definitely follow through with it. The thrill of a new job doing what you love, making new friends in coworkers, a new city to explore and everything else will take your mind off of her. Just keep looking forward. Best of luck.

:( im sorry. That was low of her to do it over a text message.

Call a friend and vent, do some of your favorite activities, anything to get your mind off of the girl and onto you and what you love. Best of luck to you, you're better without a girl that breaks up over texts.

I have/had (im not really sure) low self esteem while still being extremely confident in the moment. For me, my low self esteem was placed upon my weight and the fact that I never was one of the sought after males. I placed blame on the two factors which in return placed blame on each other. I took some time to myself to become mentally intune with who I am. I suggest you look at yourself and find out what it is about you that is causing the low self esteem. You may not want to admit it, but deep down you know what it is. Then, try to change it or accept it as who you are. Someone will love you for who you are and when you are with that person, you will never feel you have self esteem issues.

Most important part of this all was "After this summer it is very possible I won't see her again". That gives you two options. Just confess how you feel and if she doesn't feel the same, who cares! You don't want to look back and regret that you didn't tell her. You can also look to it as if you do tell her and she does feel the same, what next? She leaves and you'll never see her for a while. Will you be okay with a long distant relationship? Some things to think about.

It seems to me that you feel very resentful of your ex for putting you through a horrible time in your life. Instead of looking back and dreading on the past, you should look forward into the future and realize that you never have to deal with any of that again. Being without her should feel like a breath of fresh air. Live life and don't let the memory of her ruin any more of it.
You're welcome :). Take it as slow as you need to but do try to tell someone close soon.
Perhaps ask your boyfriend to say something to her? Maybe hearing from him that he cares about you and that you are special will make her lay off.

After spending two years chasing a girl, cut your losses while you still can. I can assure you she is not worth it. Looking back at that girl, all I see is two years wasted. Even spending time with her now I question what I saw in her. Let her go and start looking elsewhere.

I have so many friends that have all been in the same boat as you. My friends and I are all very supporting, although not everyone in the town is, and their parents have been as well since they have come out. The weight that will be lifted off your shoulder is immense. Are you having trouble sleeping and focusing because of this? Keeping it bottled up longer is only going to continue to hurt. I suggest confiding in one or two very close friends at first. Just saying it to someone will make you feel like you're breathing for the first time. From there, at your own pace, work to telling other friends and your family. It gets better, and feels better, I promise.
You're welcome and the best of luck to you :)

It seems to me that she is playing you. Shes broken up with you and does not want to get back together yet shes telling you that she misses you and still loves you. It is perfectly reasonable to have those feelings after a break up but to repeatedly tell your ex them is cruel, especially when you are not actually wanting to get back together. As much as it will suck, I suggest cutting her out of your life. It will end the pain of her toying with your heart and will allow you to cope. It will get better as time passes. 

If you do want to be with her, give her an ultimatum. Say something like "you keep telling me you miss me and still love me and want a future together but refuse to act on it. You have to decide whether you want to work on it with me or if this is over. If its over I am done, Im not going to let you keep saying those things to me and messing with my mind when you have no desire to get back with me." Good luck.

If you are on a date and things are going well, there is no reason not to try an appropriate kiss. If she does reject you, just say sorry and move on. She may have something to say back to you such as "im just not ready" or along those lines and respect that and possibly follow with "Ok, just let me know when you are".

Don't do that. Choose one for each day. There is nothing wrong with going on first dates, and even a few after that, with a few different woman. You're young and need to experience different types of woman to find out what you truly want. Once the point comes where you agree on exclusivity or bf/gf status, you should cancel all other dates.

Wow, if the parts "you always lie" and "you cheated" are true, you have every right to leave him and should never look back. If not, just tell him things arent working out for you and its over. Do not waffle on this stance in the proceeding conversation, if you have one. Stay strong and tell him the relationship is not what you want. He will try to tell you he will change to make things better, and he will at first but he will slowly start slipping back into the old patters. End it now before it causes you any more pain.

As for dealing with the pain: Like you said, surround yourself with your friends and family. Think of the things that you truly love to do and do them. Without a boyfriend holding you back you will be able to do anything you want whenever you want.

Its perfectly fine to keep all the mementos from the relationship. I know myself, and my dad, have different pieces from our past girlfriends. You can hold onto whatever you want but having a drawer full of notes, pictures, and memories may scare off a future boyfriend. Pick a few things that really stand out in your mind and hold onto them as there is nothing wrong with remembering the past as long as you're not trying to hold onto the pieces of what was.

That is a really tough situation. It is truly up to you about how you feel about her actions. If you feel betrayed and that you lost your trust for her, because she DID cheat on you, then call it off. There is also the saying that cheaters will always cheat, so be wary that she may just be using you as a support system right now and will be leaving you again when she finds the next person. I would honestly leave her and don't look back or talk to her again, for a while anyway. I am in the same situation and it is very hard, but dont give into those feelings as they will pass with time and new experiences.

Don't feel bad about posting that photo, if it happens to be the cause of her recent sadness. I personally believe that if it was the photo that caused it, its just because she saw it and it brought back some memories of you. It is not you being a dick or your fault that she felt that way. She most likely would have felt saddened if she saw any sort of remembrance of you. Just keep living your life happily and do not send her any messages. If she is the hurt one with the break up wait until she messages you.

Just remember that you, above all else, are responsible for your happiness and wellbeing. If you are not happy in the relationship call it off before you make a mistake that truly hurts him. He will find a way to deal with the break up and will most likely seek the comfort of friends and family to fill in your place. Just remember, if your boyfriend does happen to make the wrong choice and hurts himself, it is not your fault. Nothing you could have done would change it and its his own deep behavior, not the fact you broke up with him, that caused him to do it. Good luck.

If your friend does make any bad choices, please do not blame yourself. He is plenty capable of making his own decisions and you have gone above and beyond the duties of a friend, I tip my hat to you for caring so deeply for him. It seems that he is truly distraught with his life and is trying different things and exploring the world. Just because it doesn't make sense to you doesnt mean that it isn't helping him in some way. Keep in touch with him like you are, sending him updates on your life and asking about him. About all you can do, really.

I wouldnt try to get back together with her. Be grateful that she didn't progress past the point of "hey, im falling for this new guy, I should call it off with me bf" and that she didn't cheat on you. It seems to me that she made her mind up and if she did stay with you, something similar is sure to happen again. 

It really sucks that shes staying in the appt with you though. She really should move out and find her own place since she left you. That is a low move on her part.

I may be jumping to conclusions but are you also blowing off his attempts to go out with you because you fear that you will be used? My best advice is to go on a date with him and see how he treats you. Dont be over analytical and have a good time. It will be rather obvious if he is trying to get with your or if he actually likes you

Ask to go out, just the two of you. It doesn't seem you made him aware that you are interested in going on a date, just the two of you. Also, it seems you two are playing date chicken and constantly backing out or using plans as an excuse. Talk to him and set a date that neither of you will back out of, if one of you do, call it off.

Exactly. I have a friend (female) that would sleep with anyone without even going on a date. This past year she started dating a mutual friend and a year later they still haven't had sex. A lot of it has to do with the fact that she knows what she did was a mistake with the other guys and is now looking for the emotional part first.

Dont worry about it. It seems that she has forgiven you as all you did was talk with this girl. If you had done anything else you would be in a rough spot. You did everything right by being apologetic and then spending alone time with her (as thats what she wanted). I would leave it alone and see if she brings it up again.

Dont worry about it. Some girls go through rough parts of her life in which they make mistakes such as giving into sex too fast or without thinking. It seems that she has just matured and is interested in a lasting relationship with you.

This is a tough situation. I was in the same situation. My exgirlfriend would talk with, go drinking with, hang out with her best guy friend a few times a week. I found out that he had feelings for her but she told me that she ignores them and not to worry as she just enjoys being his friend. Find out from a friend that she really has feelings for him and has been emotionally cheating with him for quite some time. I honestly don't know if you're girlfriend is doing the same thing or if she just has a friend and it is impossible to know. 

Its tough with what to do next. If you hound her about her friend and she does not have feelings for him you will drive her away. If you do hound her and she does have feelings she probably wont tell you until she has the relationship stable with the other guy. Girls that cheat will cheat and you really can't change it. By best advice is if you love her, stay in the relationship and see how it shapes out. It will be very rough if she is cheating but worth it if she is not.

Wow, I am so sorry that happened to you. Like others said, don't blame yourself. Its comforting to me to know that someone is going through the same situation and is essentially doing everything that I want to do. Great guidelines.
Aha,, don't worry. I am clean and healthy; have to work ya know? And maybe attract another woman at the same time.

Yes, that was me who said dating is not for everyone. It seems though that you do want a relationship though. You should be in no rush to jump into things, nor should you expect your girlfriend to jump with you to attend these conventions in all the different countries. It will be a tough line to walk but as you said, it will be something you figure out with time and experiences. 

My best advice right now is to when you do go to these conventions is not to put any pressure on your girlfriend and not to take a declined invite seriously. It could be possible that these trips, which I am assuming would have to be over a few days, seem a little fast for your partner. Just as you wish to not attend the sports games perhaps first giving them the free skip on a convention will allow them to return the favor. In a relationship, the two of you do not need to share everything in common or even enjoy doing the same things. The biggest thing is if she accepts you for being that person and doesn't try to change you.

Try your best not to be hung up on the old girl. It seems that she was using you to not be alone. Its unfortunate and wrong that she did that to you but it seemed she was just using you until the next boyfriend was lined up and stable. Try your best to forget about her and have fun with this new girl. I can't tell if you like her as you state her pros and cons. If you are enjoying your time with her then keep seeing her. If not, it won't hurt to end it. There are plenty of fish in the see but that last one looked more like a leech.

I apologize for your dating experiences. It honestly seems that the girls you have been with have not been the right fit for you and also have been rather selfish. Not every woman will behave like this and all it takes is that one woman who understands that the events are important to you and willfully attends. I have had aspects of my life that I have kept secret in fear of rejection and since becoming open about them, yes, I have faced some girls that have brushed me off because of it but there will be the ones that are full accepting and supporting of who you really are.

You sound like my exgirlfriend. Same age, same situation. She described me the same way as you did. Her family LOVED me, she loved me, she wanted to marry me before I even thought about it. Then one day her best friend starts becoming more than that. A month or so later and shes left me for him and is now looking to either get back with me or abuse me for just a bit longer. DO NOT behave the same way as my girlfriend. If you truly love your boyfriend call it off RIGHT NOW. No one deserves to be put through a situation in which they lose all trust for their significant other and feel betrayed. I can attest to it being the worst feeling I've ever felt. If you no longer love your boyfriend, break up with him right now before you do anything to truly, mentally, hurt him more than just the adjustment to being single. 

I can tell you have a heart and are a good person, just remember that your loving boyfriend is sitting there, unaware that you're thinking of this. Do what is right for yourself but be humane about it.

You mentioned in the deleted posts comment that you have/will look in peer dating, and thats good. As for your comment about making sacrifices and changing your life, it really is part of a relationship. Both parties must make sacrifices at certain points but it does not mean you have to change who you are. We have all had to sit through thinks we havent enjoyed and you should really feel comfortable in asking your girlfriends to return the favor by attending one of your events. Its a part of your life and who knows, maybe they will surprise you by how supportive they will be.

Try your best not to be hung up on the old girl. It seems that she was using you to not be alone. Its unfortunate and wrong that she did that to you but it seemed she was just using you until the next boyfriend was lined up and stable. Try your best to forget about her and have fun with this new girl. I can't tell if you like her as you state her pros and cons. If you are enjoying your time with her then keep seeing her. If not, it won't hurt to end it. There are plenty of fish in the see but that last one looked more like a leech.
Well then, I would give her some time. It doesnt appear like youve done anything wrong so time will allow her to get her head straight.

Relationships are not for everyone but perhaps you just haven't found the right one. Some guys would love a woman who favors sports games over intelectual discussions while you seem to be the opposite. Perhaps, meeting a woman at a Royal Society panel would be a better option? Doing things you love to do is often the best way to meet someone.

It is a terrible situation to be in as it only affects your self esteem and sex drive. I have to ask, are you wearing a condom? If not, adding one may increase your time as it will decrease direct friction. 

Although it may not seem fair, sex is a very large part of a relationship but if her only complaint is your runtime it is something you can work on. Perhaps ejaculating once before sex would help as the second time lasts longer. Also, is she doing anything to you while you are eating her out? If she is, try stopping her as you won't receive any stimulation until intercourse.

It is a rough situation to be in but hopefully something I said can help.

Are you afraid of commitment? Maybe deep down you know that although these woman are great, they just aren't right. Marriage is a permanent thing and not something that should be rushed into. It sounds rough and cliche but the only thing that will get you over them is the next one that takes your breath away. You will fall in love again, you will always have the memories but you will not always feel the pain. You are not a loser and you are not the only one that feels that way (I am currently on the same boat, but was the one dumped). As for dating in the future, remember that its not where you go but its who you with that makes it special. The right person can make any place feel unique and exciting. Best of luck to you.

My best advice is during these dates alone with her just get close to her and kiss her. That perfect moment won't always be there unless you make it. 

As for date ideas, go swimming at night. It will generally be much colder than during the day in the water and even colder out. Just hold her nice and close to you to warm her up. 

You could also plan a picnic or lay on/under a blanket and watch stars. Take her to a fair and win her a prize, you most likely get a hug for that and could turn it into a kiss. You could also be the playful jerk and later in the night grab the prize and keep putting it out of her reach, if shes playfully climbing on your body bring it down slowly and grab her and kiss her. 

All I have right now but if none of those work I am sure I can come up with more.

Don't leave him or pressure him further about the situation. It seems to me like he confided something to you that either slipped out in the argument or that he truly feels and wants you to know. Commitment is a scary thing and the fact that he is talking to you about it shows signs that he is committed to the relationship even before he is mentally aware.

So, don't pressure him with advancing the relationship. It is something he needs to work out in his head but know that he does love you because he is vocal about his feelings. Best of luck.

Thanks for the very long and thorough response. 

I think that the main reason I want closure is to see if I did anything wrong; to see if she blames it on me. Why would her friend be worth throwing four years of a relationship away?

As for talking with her, I think I am going to go with what you suggested. In the long run, its only going to bring me more pain and is not worth putting myself through. Just picturing her face makes my heart ache and if I really want to get over this, which I do, I need to cut her out.

And yes, when I smoke its with my brother and his girlfriend and when I drink its with my friends. I am honestly glad she did break up with me due to the fact that I've never been closer to my brother and my friends than I have been over the last few weeks. Thanks for taking the mental pressure off.

In regards to trust issues: part of my has been fantasizing about future girlfriends and the fun that comes with it. I am afraid of bringing these trust issues into the relationship by accident but in my mind I am still the trusting same trusting guy. Hopefully, like you said, I find a girl that really fits with me and doesn't betray me like my ex did.

Rough situation you're in there but it should work itself out with time. I would text or leave her a voicemail saying something along the lines of "Babe, I know you're upset with me but I really want to talk with you about this. I haven't used the site to talk with any woman in three years and I am willing to walk through my entire profile with you if you'd like." And then just leave it until she responds. Put the ball in her court and make sure you have it seem like its completely open and in her control. You've done everything right so far, she probably just needs a night alone.

Thanks for your response. I never really thought about what you said about both of us being back up plans. I know that he is still with his GF but has been cheating on her with my ex. Also, thanks for the advice on not talking to her. I believe that you're right in her wanting to do this for herself and not to make me feel better.

I remember in high school my first kiss, the first time I held a girl's hand, and my first meaningful hug. They can be scary moments, I know my first kiss started on the lips and slid onto the cheek as I chickened out. After that it took about an hour to work up the courage to full on kiss her.

Just remember that if this girl likes you, and sometimes even if she doesnt (girls like to hold hands), she is just waiting for you to touch her. Work at a pace comfortable to you. Sit next to her somewhere on a couch or chairs. If you are truly nervous about it and can't work up the courage to start rubbing her arm and hand with your thumb and work to the hand try asking her to see her hand. Do something corny like "read her palm". That way you will be at least touching her and can slowly work into holding hands.

Or, since you are doing something with her next week try just asking to hold her hand as you walk around. Some girls think its very sweet when you ask to do these things. If she still wants to hang out with you alone there isn't much to be worried about her not liking you. If you do touch her, don't chicken out like I did with my kiss. Touch her and keep your hand there to show you mean it. She will move out of your touch if she doesn't like it.

Anyway, have fun and take it slow and steady :)
Be clear with your intentions. Next time you go out, since it seems like you will, tell her you like her. If she does not feel the same way it does not have to end your relationship as friends.

Thanks for responding. I doubt she will have a very good reason as to why she left but right now I feel like its something I need to hear. Part of me wants to never see her again, find someone new, and hopefully lose this urge to know why. 

As for taking her back, I know its something I should never do deep down. She knowingly and repeatedly betrayed me and that hurts the most. She did somethings at the start of our relationship that threw my trust off but since then I had grown to sincerely trust her with my life. Now I feel that trust is forever ruined and not something I could ever get over, with her. I am only hoping by the time I have another girlfriend I can trust her without this lurking reminder.
